correctness.rationale: C: Strict positivity forbids empty bundles in an EFX allocation with m=n+2, so only one triple or two double bundles are possible. Sorting four smallest goods a>=b>=c>=d, triple shape succeeds for the bottom triple if a>=b+c, and double shape with (a,d)|(b,c) succeeds if a<=b+c. Thus a uniform surjection always has at least n! successes among n![C(m,3)+3C(m,4)] allocations. Symmetrization of any value-independent lottery preserves/improves worst-case success; adversarial bottom values (10,4,3,1) and (6,4,3,1), all other values larger, force exclusively one triple or one double pairing, giving upper min(t/C(m,3),d0/[3C(m,4)])<=1/H. Independent exhaustive EFX allocation recomputation for n=2,m=4 reproduced exactly two winning labelled allocations in each adversarial case, one occupancy type each. Boundary n=2 and tie permissiveness follow from inequalities; infinite n uses the proof.
